topic: How one request travels: client to API to database, and how to use that map to find bugs faster
save_reason: A one-slide bug map that matches each HTTP status code to the part to check (client, API or database), shown on the cheat sheet and in full in the caption.
send_reason: Send this to a friend building their first full-stack app.

cover.concept: Retro tech still life on a wooden desk: a 1980s beige keyboard, a beige desktop modem with small green lights and a grey metal card-index drawer, joined left to right by one coiled cable.
hooks: Trace one click to the database and back. (curiosity)
Every full-stack app has the same three parts. (awe)
Find any bug faster with this one map. (confidence)
Explain your project like an engineer in interviews. (ambition)

slides.label: Step 1: client
slides.idea: The browser (client) sends the request: a React form calls fetch with the email and password.
slides.title: Your browser sends the request first.

slides.label: Step 2: API
slides.idea: Break a belief: the frontend never talks to the database directly; the API checks every request in between.
slides.title: Your frontend never talks to the database directly.
slides.line: The API sits in between and checks every request.
slides.screen: Code editor cropped big: fictional Express route app.post('/api/login', ...) that checks the email is present, then calls the database

slides.label: Step 3: database
slides.idea: Not A or B, it's C: the data lives in the database; the API asks it and sends the answer back.
slides.title: It's not the browser or the API that stores it.
slides.line: It's the database, and the API asks it for data.

Bug map
200: it worked
400: check what the client sent
401: check the login
404: check the URL and the API route
500: check the API and database logs
